original_question: Determine whether there exists a II1 factor N such that the ultrapower NU has non-full fundamental group.
target_in_paper: Miscellaneous, Problem 48: Does there exist a II_1 factor N such that N^𝒰 has non-full fundamental group?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it asks for the existence of a II_1 factor, it focuses on the ultrapower/tracial ultrapower of that factor, and it singles out the same property in Problem 48, namely having non-full fundamental group.
missing_details: The paper fixes a non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ at the outset; the intended object is N^𝒰 with respect to that fixed ultrafilter, not an unspecified ultrapower.
The relevant construction is the tracial ultrapower of a tracial von Neumann algebra, so the notation should be N^𝒰 rather than the ambiguous 'NU'.

To make the question stand-alone, 'non-full fundamental group' should be unpacked as saying that the fundamental group of N^𝒰 is not all of the positive reals under multiplication, i.e. F(N^𝒰) ≠ R_{>0}.
If full self-containment is desired, the fundamental group should be defined explicitly as F(P) = { t > 0 : P^t ≅ P } for a II_1 factor P.
No extra assumptions such as separability, Connes embeddability, McDuffness, or being a group factor appear in the paper's formulation, so none should be added.
refined_question: Fix the non-principal ultrafilter 𝒰 on ℕ used throughout the paper. Does there exist a II_1 factor N such that its tracial ultrapower N^𝒰 has non-full fundamental group; equivalently, such that F(N^𝒰) = { t > 0 : (N^𝒰)^t ≅ N^𝒰 } is a proper subgroup of the positive real multiplicative group?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 48 in the Miscellaneous section. The only paper-specific notation needed to make your draft fully stand-alone is supplied in the opening notation paragraph: 𝒰 is fixed to be a non-principal ultrafilter on ℕ, and M^𝒰 denotes the tracial ultrapower of a tracial von Neumann algebra M. So your draft already captures the correct mathematical target, but it leaves implicit the ultrafilter, the tracial-ultrapower notation, and the standard meaning of 'non-full fundamental group.' I did not add any separability or embeddability assumptions because the paper does not.
